simcc-simoc-2022-g1-01.title: Look at the last digit
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-01.body:
An odd number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9. Only 441 does.

**Answer: (C) 441**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-02.title: Balance the numbers
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-02.body:
13 changes to 4, which is 9 less. So the first number must be 9 more: $8+9=17$.

**Answer: (C) 17**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-03.title: Turn every card into a number
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-03.body:
38, 38, 30, 39, 35. The greatest is 39.

**Answer: (D) 3 tens and 9 ones**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-05.title: Pair them up
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-05.body:
Pair $5-4=1$, $9-8=1$, $13-12=1$, $17-16=1$. That gives 4. With the 2 left over, the answer is $4+2=6$.

**Answer: (B) 6**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-06.title: Multiply, then subtract
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-06.body:
6 boxes have $6\times4=24$ cookies. After eating 1, he has $24-1=23$.

**Answer: (C) 23**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-07.title: Use the second line
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-07.body:
Two teddy bears cost \$56, so one bear costs $56\div2=\$28$. A bear and a car cost \$50, so the car costs $50-28=\$22$.

**Answer: (C) \$22**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-08.title: Count small to big
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-08.body:
Call the corners of the figure top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left, and let O be the point in the middle where all three lines cross.

- 4 small triangles: each has O as a corner and a short piece of a slanted side of the figure as its base (two above the horizontal line and two below it).
- 4 medium triangles: each has O as a corner and a whole side of the figure as its base (top, bottom, left and right sides).
- 4 big triangles: each is half of the figure, cut off by one of the two long slanted lines.

$4+4+4=12$.

**Answer: (B) 12**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-09.title: Count column by column
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-09.body:
Look at the pile as a grid of columns and count the cubes in each column, starting from the corner against the walls. The heights are, row by row: $4,3,2,1$ then $3,3,2,1$ then $2,2,1$.

Add them: $4+3+2+1=10$, then $3+3+2+1=9$, then $2+2+1=5$. The total is $10+9+5=24$.

**Answer: (E) 24**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-10.title: Two rulers is six pens
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-10.body:
One ruler is 3 pens, so two rulers are 6 pens. Two pens are 5 pencils, so 6 pens are 3 groups of 2 pens, which is $3\times5=15$ pencils.

**Answer: (C) 15 pencils**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-11.title: Count the digits used
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-11.body:
The first three cards use 8, 2, 9, 3, 9, 8, 5, 6, 3. So 8, 9 and 3 are already used twice. Each digit appears exactly twice in all four numbers, so the fourth card must use the digits that have been used only once: 2, 5 and 6.

The smallest number from 2, 5, 6 is 256.

**Answer: (E) 256**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-12.title: Use Dorothy as the base
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-12.body:
Say Dorothy is $D$. Benjamin is $D-4$, Amy is $D-2$, Cindy is $D-3$. Amy plus Cindy is $2D-5=17$, so $2D=22$ and $D=11$.

Ages: Dorothy 11, Benjamin 7, Amy 9, Cindy 8. Sum: $11+7+9+8=35$.

**Answer: (D) 35**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-12.title: Try ages
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-12.body:
Amy is 2 older than Benjamin and Benjamin is 4 younger than Dorothy, so Amy is 2 younger than Dorothy. Cindy is 3 younger. Together Amy and Cindy are 5 younger than 2 Dorothys, so 2 Dorothys are 22, and Dorothy is 11. The rest follow: 9, 8, 7. Total 35.

**Answer: (D) 35**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-14.title: Large digits only
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-14.body:
The largest digit sum for 3 digits is 27 (999). To get 25 we need to lose 2 from 27. Either one digit drops by 2 (to 7) or two digits drop by 1 each (to 8).

- one 7 and two 9s: 799, 979, 997 (3 numbers)
- two 8s and one 9: 889, 898, 988 (3 numbers)

Total $3+3=6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-15.title: Even multiples of 5 end in 0
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-15.body:
A multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5, and it is even only if it ends in 0. So we count the multiples of 10 up to 202: 10, 20, ..., 200. That is 20 numbers.

**Answer: (B) 20**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-17.title: Put in the value
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-17.body:
The equation says $(\triangle-1)\times(\triangle+1)=35$. The two numbers differ by 2 and multiply to 35: $5\times7=35$. So $\triangle-1=5$ and $\triangle=6$.

**Answer: 6**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-18.title: Find the rule
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-18.body:
In the first circle: $13+17-5=25$. Second: $15+14-10=19$. Third: $24+19-11=32$. So the middle is the two upper numbers added, minus the bottom number.

Last circle: $9+7-5=11$.

**Answer: 11**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-19.title: Total of all faces
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-19.body:
Each cube has three pairs of opposite faces, each pair adding to 7, so one cube's faces add to $3\times7=21$. Two cubes: $42$.

The five visible faces add to $2+1+3+4+5=15$. The other 7 faces add to $42-15=27$.

**Answer: 27**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-20.title: Work with fractions of the total
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-20.body:
After sharing, half is left. After eating 13, one-third is left. So 13 cookies are the difference between one half and one third of the total. That is one sixth. So one sixth is 13 and the total is $6\times13=78$.

**Answer: 78**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-20.title: Check
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-20.body:
78: half is 39 shared, 39 left. $39-13=26$, which is one third of 78. It works.

**Answer: 78**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-21.title: Cross multiply
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-21.body:
Take the four corner numbers. In the first shape, top-left $\times$ bottom-right plus top-right $\times$ bottom-left: $1\times2+2\times5=12$. Second: $3\times3+4\times2=17$. Third: $2\times2+5\times4=24$. The rule works.

Last shape: $2\times3+5\times5=6+25=31$.

**Answer: 31**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-22.title: Two clues
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-22.body:
The number is in the 9 times table. And one less than the number is in the 10 times table, so it ends in 1. Look at the 9 times table: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81. The first one ending in 1 is 81.

Check: $81-1=80=10\times8$.

**Answer: 81**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-23.title: Count digits in groups
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-23.body:
Pages 1 to 9 use 9 digits. The remaining $99-9=90$ digits are used by 2-digit page numbers, 2 digits each, so $90\div2=45$ more pages. The last page is $9+45=54$.

**Answer: 54**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-24.title: Ones place and tens place
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-24.body:
Ones place: 2, 12, 22, ..., 132. These are 14 numbers.

Tens place: 20 to 29 (10 numbers) and 120 to 129 (10 numbers), so 20 times.

The number 22 is counted twice (once in each place) and that is right, because it has two 2s. The hundreds digit is never 2.

Total $14+20=34$.

**Answer: 34**

simcc-simoc-2022-g1-25.title: Try Cindy as the truth-teller
simcc-simoc-2022-g1-25.body:
Suppose Cindy always tells the truth. Then there are 13 candies, and that is more than Amy's 9, which fits. Now Frank said Cindy only tells the truth (true) and 18 candies (false): one truth and one lie. Amy said 9 candies (false) and Frank always lies (false): always lies. Everything fits: one truth-teller, one liar, one mixed.

There are 13 candies.

**Answer: 13**
